name: STORM R1 clincher

origin.basis: ARISUN is a ZC Rubber (Zhongce, maker of Chaoyang) bicycle-tire brand; the official listing gives the brand as 朝阳 and the item code 艾瑞森H-908.

manufacturing.basis: The listing does not state the factory location.

positioning: ZC Rubber's lightweight 330 TPI folding race clincher, sold in China as a lower-priced alternative to premium race tires.
weight_basis: One owner weighed a 28C clincher at 221 g; the official listing gives 215 g without a size.

wet_notes.summary: In a tire seller's post, one commenter found it grippier than a GP5000 in the rain after two months; the seller's own wet warning is not an owner test.
An owner who did not say clincher or tubeless reported slips on puddles and road paint and replaced the tires.

community.summary: Light and lively for 3,000 km; a bulge formed at a puncture site, and commenters reported sidewall cord cracks at 100-1,000 km.
A creator test presents it as a GP5000 alternative; commenters reported early cracks and bulges, some replaced under warranty.
Owner-measured 221 g at 28C; commenters praise speed and feel but report fast wear.
About 10,000 km to the casing for a light rider with about five punctures; the post does not say clincher or tubeless.

availability.note: Sold in mainland China through an official Tmall store; no European or North American seller was verified.

price_observations.conditions: Tmall list price before discounts ('优惠前') on 2026-11-01; the listing does not say whether the option is one tire or a pair.

caveats: Clincher owners report anything from a sidewall crack after about 1,000 km and a rear worn through at 1,800 km to 8,000 km of use; inspect the casing regularly.
Wet grip is unresolved: the few owner wet reports conflict, the slip report does not say clincher or tubeless, and no lab or controlled wet-braking test was found.
Mount in the direction of the rotation arrow, which some owners say is opposite to Continental's.
The official store price is CNY 268 per listing option; whether an option is one tire or a pair is not stated.

image.shown: Folded 28C STORM R1 clincher on a scale (221.5 g) in an owner's post; the sidewall reads ARISUN STORM R1, ULTRA 330 TPI.
image.alt: Folded ARISUN STORM R1 road tire with its sidewall label, weighed on a kitchen scale

rights.usage_note: A photo from a public Xiaohongshu post, shown from Xiaohongshu with a link to the original post; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded from seven Xiaohongshu posts and their visible comments, reviewed on 2026-11-03 (not exhaustive). Counted only owners who said they ride the clincher or whose stated 28 mm weight is the clincher's; replies that did not say clincher or tubeless, seller replies, questions, hearsay, prices and repeated comments by one owner were left out. Two later comparison threads were added on 2026-11-03. Four posts remain as post notes: three older posts whose commenters have not been checked owner by owner, and a 10,000 km report that does not say clincher or tubeless.

reports.exposure: Rear about 1,800 km in two months; front about 6,000 km in five months
reports.summary: The rear wore through to the casing after about 1,800 km while the front was still fine at about 6,000 km; the owner summed it up as getting what you pay for.
Found it too hard: the rear stepped out when cornering on descents, so the owner switched to Michelin tires. Road conditions not stated.

reports.exposure: Over 3,000 km in about a year
reports.summary: Hard-wearing: the front still showed its centre line after more than 3,000 km. Fine surface cracks appeared after a year, but the owner expects another year of use.
Ridden with a TPU tube: very good value and no flat in 3,000 km.
After a first 70 km it felt lighter to accelerate and about 1 km/h faster at the same effort than the stock tires; not a controlled test.
More dry-road grip and high-speed stability than a Michelin Power Cup and comfortable, but slower to spin up; called it good value. Not yet ridden in the wet.
No problem so far after about 2,000 km.
The rear sidewall cracked and the tire was scrapped after just over 1,000 km.
Punctured several times and was replaced after 7,000 km.
Has ridden 8,000 km on the clincher.
Finds the clincher fine in use; the same owner gave up on the tubeless version early.
In an uncontrolled five-tire comparison the 230 g 28 mm tire, the clincher's weight, rolled best and came third of five for grip.
Chose the clincher rather than tubeless for a new wheelset: quick to accelerate, rolls freely and holds well in sharp corners, though it is harsher over bumps at the owner's high pressure.

checks.note: Nine posts; three older posts are not yet re-checked owner by owner
